images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of Align Then Reason (atr).Stage 1 (Align):the silent mouth video is encoded into frame embeddings𝐡1:T\mathbf{h}_{1:T}and the candidate line into phonetic-unit embeddings𝐮1:N\mathbf{u}_{1:N}. Their similarityMt,nM_{t,n}is scored by CTC whose labels are thepositionsof the units in the line, so only a monotonic path throughMM(highlighted) scores well, and reordering, shifting, or freezing the frames breaks it. Trained with content and temporal negatives, the scorer emits a calibrated global scorea⁡(V,c)a(V,c)and per-unit soft tokens𝐞soft1:N\mathbf{e}^{\mathrm{soft}}_{1:N}.Stage 2 (Reason):the soft tokens are prepended to a prompt containinga⁡(V,c)a(V,c)and the line, and an LLM answers whether the mouth matches the line; the difference of itsYesandNologits is the lip-sync score.
